title: Bounded local project-test shard optimization
rawUserRequest: The user authorized continuous execution until the remaining Work Items are genuinely closed. For this Work Item, improve the local project-test performance after the parallel-processing lessons, while preserving complete test ownership, evidence integrity, existing coverage thresholds, and the requirement that completion evidence be measured rather than inferred.

declaredIntent.summary: Reduce local project-test wall time with bounded, source-bound sharding while preserving every governed verification and evidence boundary.

riskAssessment.reason: Local quality execution is currently serial and resource-bound. Bounded sharding can reduce wall time, but concurrent shard outputs, coverage combination, exact source identity, and failure diagnostics must remain deterministic and fail closed.

reasons: This changes a governed quality gate and its evidence boundary.

preReviewWarnings: Review that the default local path executes every manifest entry exactly once across bounded shards.
Review that aggregate coverage, critical coverage, shell boundaries, and receipts remain fail closed.
Review performance claims only against same-base comparable timing evidence; do not infer a general speedup from one environment.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record the implementation checkpoint before editing and a strict pre-finish checkpoint after comparable timing and regression evidence are available.

acceptance: The default local `make project-test` path uses the existing source-bound manifest and runs its five balanced shards with an explicit bounded concurrency limit, then performs the existing aggregate coverage, critical-coverage, and receipt gates; coverage path aliases bind isolated shard sources to the repository source tree, aggregate JSON tolerates unavailable ephemeral fixture sources, and the 85.10 floor remains enforced after shard cleanup.

Every manifest entry is owned by exactly one shard; shard, aggregate, and receipt evidence bind the current commit/tree/manifest/plan and fail closed on missing, failed, duplicate, or mismatched evidence.
The existing 85.10 coverage floor and installer/CI-release boundary checks remain enforced without omission, weakening, or duplicate execution.
Focused regression tests cover the Make DAG, all five shard aliases, exact manifest ownership, failure diagnostics, and aggregate receipt identity.

A same-base serial baseline and candidate local timing are captured with the performance-diagnosis evidence rules; any improvement claim is limited to the measured environment and makes no causal or general claim without comparable evidence.
English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese quality-gate documentation state the bounded local shard behavior and its boundary from hosted CI and adopter-owned project test commands.
The Work Item completes the strict AI lifecycle, generated status, outcome pair, archive, PR, hosted checks, merge, and close-work-item sequence.

guidelines: Preserve the existing source-bound manifest, shard, aggregate, receipt, coverage, and critical-boundary checks.
Do not import internal modules from unrelated features or introduce a second test ownership mechanism.
Document public Make targets and the local-versus-hosted/adopter execution boundary in all maintained locales.
Do not claim performance improvement beyond comparable measured evidence.

intent.problem: The repository's local project-test gate remains serial even though the source-bound manifest and hosted five-shard topology already provide a bounded, auditable execution model. The resulting quality feedback is slow and has been observed as a practical performance bottleneck.
constraints: No test ownership, coverage threshold, evidence identity, or failure diagnostics may be weakened.
Hosted CI topology and adopter-owned PROJECT_TEST commands are reference boundaries, not this Work Item's implementation surface.
Historical archive evidence is immutable; any correction must be delivered by a successor Work Item.
All quality verification must be serialized when full-repository resource contention would otherwise invalidate evidence.
intent.rationale: Reuse the existing manifest/shard/aggregate infrastructure, expose a bounded local Make DAG, and verify exact ownership plus same-base timing so efficiency improves without trading away trust.
